title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's future uncertain as Megaspeed pledges to co-operate with U.S. probe

image.caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks to the media and attendees after a reception celebrating the U.K.'s technology ecosystem and AI advances in London on Oct. 14, 2026. (Kwiyeon Ha/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Business·New
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's future as the leader of the chip-making giant he co-founded is uncertain, as the company board discusses potential replacements amid a widening personal scandal.
Nvidia has said it had 'no reason to believe' that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised

Nvidia's board of directors is reportedly meeting to discuss CEO Jensen Huang's future after revelations that he was having an affair with a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese government agent.
There was no word as of early Thursday on any outcome from those discussions.
Nasdaq-listed Nvidia shares tumbled nearly nine per cent in pre-market trading on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Megaspeed, the data centre company at the heart of the scandal engulfing Huang, pledged Thursday to co-operate with an investigation into potential risks to U.S. national security.

blocks.text: The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports.

In its first statement since the scandal broke, Singapore-headquartered Megaspeed International said on Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws "extremely seriously."
Details about Huang's affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear.
"Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government," said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
Nvidia has said it had "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Trump says FBI investigating

Details about Huang's affair with the woman are unclear. The New York Times reported she was Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le, and was a top executive at Megaspeed. The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. The two are not related.

Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia's Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating.

Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was "no evidence" of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations.

China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world's most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. In January, he won Trump's approval for selling its H200 chips to China.

In its statement on Thursday, Megaspeed said it has co-operated with the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on exports of technology, and was ready to "co-operate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority."
It said it has hired a U.S. law firm to handle a "comprehensive census" of its computer chips and to verify its export controls.

"Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws," it said.

Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed's finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost $3 billion US, according to Singapore corporate records.
Revenue surged to over $294 million US in 2024 from none in 2023.
